minutes.headline: Parks Commission dropped season beach passes and cut daily half-day rates for the season, by roll call vote.
minutes.summary: The commission met remotely on the eve of the beach opening. It heard that the board of health still had not returned the water sample or approved application. It then voted to offer only half-day passes at lower rates, with no season pass. Members also discussed day-pass tracking, the cap on beach capacity, and the pending charter to expand the commission to five members.

public_comment.topic: Status of the town charter in the state House (Senate bill S 2754), needed to expand the commission to five members; urged residents to contact representatives.

votes.motion: Adjust half-day pass rates to three dollars per adult and two dollars per child, and offer only half-day passes with no season pass.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; the three members each voiced aye)

budget_items.topic: Electronic card/swipe system for beach attendance
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said an electronic system would give the only accurate data on beach use. Staff said issuing cards to every day-pass user was not feasible for a part-time director.

budget_items.topic: Season pass versus daily pass pricing
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff compared losing a daily fee with losing the season pass fee, saying both would be non-refundable.

budget_items.topic: Family season pass fee and add-ons
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff suggested keeping the family pass price the same as past years, with an extra fee per additional household member.
Current rates were stated, and a member proposed lowering them.

budget_items.topic: Revenue per session at lower rates
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair worked through revenue at the capacity cap against the cost of three lifeguards, and a member accepted possible operating deficit.
The motion set adult and child half-day rates and no season pass.

decisions.decision: Fees cut to adult and child half-day rates for the season; no season pass offered.
Staff asked to prepare a step-by-step registration guide for the senior center to send to seniors.
Electronic card tracking deferred to next year; this year staff use pre-registration and rosters.
No vote taken on delaying the opening, since the board of health controls it; opening stays Monday pending approval.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted by roll call to offer only half-day beach passes at lower adult and child rates, with no season pass.
The fee change applies for the season; no season pass will be sold.
The board of health had not yet returned the water sample or approved the beach application, so the opening stays Monday pending approval; no vote was taken to delay it.
Electronic card tracking of beach attendance was deferred to next year; staff will use pre-registration and rosters this year.
Staff were asked to prepare a step-by-step registration guide for the senior center to send to seniors.

why_it_matters: Families who would have bought a season pass can now only pay per half-day visit, and the lower rates may leave the beach's operating cost, including lifeguards, partly uncovered by fees.
Opening still depends on a board of health approval, so beach access on the planned date is not yet certain.
watch_next: Board of health approval of the water sample and beach application, which the opening depends on.
The town charter bill in the state House (Senate bill S 2754), needed to expand the commission to five members.
